import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import io
import seaborn as sns

# Dataset provided as a string
data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Convert 'has_video_4k' to a descriptive categorical type for better legend readability
df['has_video_4k_label'] = df['has_video_4k'].map({0: 'No 4K Video', 1: 'Has 4K Video'})

# Set up the matplotlib figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8)) # Increased figure size for better readability

# Create a scatter plot using seaborn to visualize relationships
# - x-axis: Megapixels (resolution)
# - y-axis: Price (USD)
# - hue: Color points by Sensor Type (e.g., Micro 4/3, APS-C, Full Frame, Medium Format)
# - style: Use different marker styles based on 4K Video capability (Yes/No)
# - size: Vary marker size by Weight (grams), indicating physical bulk
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    style='has_video_4k_label',
    size='weight_grams',
    sizes=(100, 1000), # Define the range of marker sizes for weight
    palette='tab10', # A distinct color palette for sensor types
    alpha=0.8, # Slightly transparent points for potential overlap (though unlikely with 5 points)
    legend='full' # Ensure all legends (hue, style, size) are displayed and managed by seaborn
)

# Add brand labels next to each point for easy identification, given the small dataset
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    plt.text(row['megapixels'] + 0.7, # Offset X-coordinate slightly
             row['price_usd'] + 70,  # Offset Y-coordinate slightly
             row['brand'],
             horizontalalignment='left',
             verticalalignment='bottom',
             size='small',
             color='black',
             weight='semibold') # Make text bold for better visibility

# Add titles and labels for clarity
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels, by Sensor Type, 4K Video, and Weight', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels and legends from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png')
